clue.text: Perhaps lied in advance, for modular construction?

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: describing buildings put together from factory-made modules

parts.note: the prefix PRE- means beforehand or in advance
to have lied is to have made a story up, so 'perhaps' flags a loose sense: invented, made up

explanation.surface: A wry question: is a building of modules just a lie told ahead of time?
explanation.walkthrough: Fabricated means both 'lied about' and 'manufactured', which is the pun the clue turns on.
explanation.definitionFit: Buildings assembled on site from units made beforehand in a factory are described by this adjective, a modular method of building.

clue.text: Up-market Post Office shut up

parts.note: SH is the hushing call telling someone to be quiet

explanation.surface: An upmarket post office has been closed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal synonyms for smart, expensive and aimed at wealthy customers.

clue.text: Toenail broken in high spirits

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces that can be reassembled, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone oddly cheerful despite a broken toenail.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a feeling of great happiness and exhilaration is what high spirits describes.

clue.text: Audibly, verbally given permission

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so the word for the following phrase is to be taken as it sounds when said

parts.note: to be given permission is to be allowed

explanation.surface: Someone granted permission out loud rather than in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: done audibly means done so as to be heard, out loud rather than silently.

clue.text: Witty comeback in regard to wrongful act

parts.note: RE means concerning or in regard to, as in a letter's subject line
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A sharp reply made concerning some wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: TORT is the legal term for a civil wrong that gives grounds for a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a quick, sharp or witty reply to a remark is a comeback.

clue.text: Happen on area with harvester, to fail completely

parts.note: to come about is to happen, so come stands for happen
a cropper is one who gathers or cuts a crop

explanation.surface: A farmer chances on a field with a harvesting machine, only for it to end badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come a cropper' is an informal British idiom meaning to fall heavily or fail badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase means to suffer a heavy fall or a total, humiliating failure.

clue.text: Lure embodied in "caveat emptor"

indicators.note: something embodied in a phrase is contained within it, so the letters sit inside the quoted words

explanation.surface: A lure is the very spirit of 'let the buyer beware'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to entice or attract someone, often towards something unwise.

clue.text: Dig up established edition, having no personal stake

parts.note: to disinter is to dig up something buried
EST is the abbreviation for established, as on shop signs

explanation.surface: An impartial reviewer unearths a long-standing edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: impartial, unbiased because one has nothing to gain or lose.

clue.text: Physical game involving each coastal settlement

indicators.note: involving here means wrapping round, so the second word goes inside the first

parts.note: a sport is a physical game

explanation.surface: Every harbour town is playing some rough contact sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A town with a harbour where ships dock is a kind of coastal settlement.

clue.text: Addition to letter after mother's disease

indicators.note: after places the postscript behind the word for mother

parts.note: MUM is the British word for mother
PS, postscript, is something added to a letter

explanation.surface: A postscript reports that Mother has caught an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a contagious viral disease causing swelling of the glands in the neck.

clue.text: Nursery school, more gentle, cultivated great name

parts.note: kinder means more gentle

indicators.note: cultivated soil is worked over, so the letters of the next word are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A school where a gentler, cultivated name is grown.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a school or class for very young children before formal schooling.

clue.text: Quickly saw head of government told untruths about politicians

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
about means surrounding, so the word for untruths goes round the politicians

parts.note: lied means told untruths
MPs are Members of Parliament, i.e. politicians

explanation.surface: The prime minister briefly saw that the leader lied about MPs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of government' looks like the prime minister, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have seen briefly or partially, caught a fleeting look.

clue.text: Chance to identify criminal dose of cocaine in court

parts.note: a line is a dose of cocaine laid out for snorting
UP means appearing in court, as in 'up before the magistrate'

explanation.surface: A drug offender is in court, where witnesses may pick him out.
explanation.definitionFit: An identity parade, where witnesses pick a suspect from a row of people.

clue.text: University transaction is far from perfect

parts.note: a deal is a business transaction

explanation.surface: A university's deal turns out to be unsatisfactory.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally not ideal: an adjective for something falling short of the best.

clue.text: Where one might find shops are protecting blackguard

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding as a shield, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a blackguard

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers shield a scoundrel among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A covered walkway lined with shops, so one place shops are found.

clue.text: Clear guilt of able-bodied seaman, very into flatfish

indicators.note: into places the abbreviation for very inside the fish

parts.note: a sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A sailor who is very keen on flatfish is cleared of blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to declare someone free from blame or sin, to acquit.

clue.text: English physicist from modern century?

parts.note: new means modern
a ton is a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: Is a recent century's scientist the subject here?
explanation.walkthrough: Isaac Newton, who described gravity, was an English physicist.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Isaac Newton, the seventeenth-century scientist of gravity and motion.

clue.text: Propelled weapon to fail to hit French island

parts.note: to miss is to fail to hit
ile is the French word for island

explanation.surface: A projectile fired at a French island misses its target.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an object or rocket that is thrown or fired at a target.

clue.text: I suffer without complaining 'cos it is different

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters of the phrase before are put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone explains they endure quietly because they are not like others.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who bears hardship without grumbling could say this of themself.

clue.text: Stick English after History?

indicators.note: after sends the abbreviation for English behind the word for history

parts.note: history is the past

explanation.surface: Should English be studied after History in the timetable?
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to glue or fix something in place with an adhesive.

clue.text: Small cake's small pointed shape

parts.note: a cone is a shape tapering to a point

explanation.surface: A little cake baked in a tiny pointed shape.
explanation.walkthrough: A scone is a small British baked item, like an American biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small, plain, lightly sweetened baked item eaten with butter or cream.

clue.text: Type of racing Los Angeles's seen in robbery

indicators.note: seen in means appearing inside, so the city goes within the word for robbery

parts.note: theft is robbery

explanation.surface: Los Angeles turns up in a heist at a horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flat is British horse racing run without jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind of horse racing over a course with no fences or hurdles.

clue.text: Line used in avoiding young bird

indicators.note: used in means put inside, so the line goes within the word for avoiding

parts.note: ducking means dodging or avoiding

explanation.surface: A fishing line is used to dodge a chick.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the young of a duck is one kind of young bird.

clue.text: Flex book to finish

parts.note: end means finish

explanation.surface: A command to bend a book's spine until it gives out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to curve or bow something, as you would a limb or a strip of metal.
